change: Copy retained scrollback cells in contiguous spans while preserving delayed wrapping, every cell attribute and the existing bounded history ring. Main-screen cursor mapping retains scalar appends.
scope: Isolated native C terminal resize and history reflow using the maintained capture_replay benchmark. Excludes replay, transport, UI and display. Same generated files except scalar versus contiguous history-cell transfers.
compiler: cc -std=c11 -O2; identical flags for both generated C fixtures
metric: Median of two per-run mean resize/reflow times; 250 repetitions per case in each run. Individual operation latency percentiles were not measured.
checks: 45 scalar/reference stream cases across 256 span boundaries each, in source and saved-IR C/C++ execution
Full capture replay parity in source and saved-IR C/C++: Unicode, attributes, wrap boundaries, history limits, later feeds and width changes
Cursor reflow and cursor metadata checks in C/C++; portable metadata also in Go and source/saved VM execution
Full capture replay parity in source and saved-IR native Plan 9 8c/8l execution in private QEMU
limits: Isolated resize/reflow results, not full Harmony interaction latency.
The 24-line, 32-column case was approximately 2% slower; no speedup claimed for that case.
No additional buffers or history limits were introduced; RAM/CPU reduction and other platform performance have not been measured.
